newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber rallies sharply on commercial demand.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber rallies sharply on commercial demand.

text.p: CME lumber futures ran up sharply as commercial demand and short covering erased early losses and the limit decline of $10.00 per tbf in November.

Initial carryover sell stops pushed November down the limit before prices turned higher led by September. Commercial buying and mixed short covering in September prompted demand in other months, traders said.

Traders noted that although cash spruce was quoted unchanged at $432 per tbf, demand for product remains strong. September is a good buy as it equals $406 cost after deduction for shipping costs, one source noted.
Rolling of short positions from September into November kept some scaleup pressure on November, they added.

November opened limit down at $364.50 per tbf and then moved up to post a loss of $2.00 at $372.50 in latest trade. Limitless September rallied as much as $9.90 and is currently up $8.00 at $416.00 per tbf. Other months are up $4.00 to $6.90 per tbf.
